---
title: "04 · Anisotropy and nonlinear excess"
description: "Distinguish distance-value recovery from arbitrary-feature recovery."
---

For covariance eigenvalues `lambda_j`, the best rank-`m` recovery of the
distance value captures the leading share of squared-eigenvalue mass:

$$\alpha_m=\frac{\sum_{j\le m}\lambda_j^2}{\sum_j\lambda_j^2}.$$

That statement does **not** automatically bound every nonlinear feature. Unequal
retention across eigenspaces can create nonlinear excess. Equal fractional
retention across every spectral block restores the clean ceiling.

```python
import numpy as np
from rpgeom.ceilings import alpha_m, alpha_pi
print(alpha_m(np.array([4., 1., 1., 1.]), m=1))
print(alpha_pi(lam=[4., 1.], r=[20, 40], s=[5, 10]))
```
